**19** Remember my suffering and my aimless wandering — the bitterness and the poison.

**20** I will never forget this dreadful time, as my soul sinks within me.

**21** Yet I still dare to hope when I remember this:

**22** The faithful love of the LORD never ends! His mercies never stop.

**23** They are new every morning. How great is Your faithfulness!

**24** I say to myself, "The LORD is my inheritance; therefore, I will hope in Him!"

**25** The LORD is good to those who depend on Him, to those who search for Him.

**26** It is good to wait quietly for salvation from the LORD.

**27** It is good for people to submit to the yoke of discipline while they are young.

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **3:1-18**: Before hope comes, the poet catalogs every form of suffering imaginable. He doesn't rush to the good part. Authentic hope requires honest grief.

- **3:22-23**: These two verses — 'His mercies are new every morning' — sit in the middle of the darkest book in the Bible. Hope doesn't eliminate the darkness; it exists within it.

- **3:27**: Bearing the yoke while young — suffering teaches endurance. Not 'everything happens for a reason,' but 'even this can form something in you.'

— PNEUMA
